I searched CPRD for "eosinophilic oesophagitis", "eosinophilic esophagitis", "eosinophil", "oesophag eosin", "EoE" and "allergic oesophagitis", and looked up all codes starting with J101 (the oesophagitis group). Four codes indicate the condition.

## Codelist: Eosinophilic oesophagitis

| Code | Term | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| J1017 | Eosinophilic oesophagitis | Read v2 |
| ^ESCTEO508265 | Eosinophilic esophagitis | SNOMED CT (EMIS term code) |
| ^ESCT1165474 | Food-induced eosinophilic oesophagitis | SNOMED CT (EMIS term code) |
| ^ESCTEO508286 | Eosinophilic ulcer of oesophagus | SNOMED CT (EMIS term code) |

**What I chose to leave out:**
- **Other eosinophilic gut conditions:** eosinophilic gastritis (^ESCTEO357862), gastroenteritis (^ESCTEO620672), duodenitis (^ESCTEO776367), enteritis (^ESCTEO795465 and ^ESCT1458627) and colitis (^ESCTEO296828). These are different conditions further down the gut, so they don't show that someone has eosinophilic oesophagitis.
- **Hypereosinophilic syndrome and general eosinophilia codes:** these are blood or whole-body conditions, not oesophageal ones.
- **Other oesophagitis codes** (reflux, ulcerative, chemical and unspecified oesophagitis, J101/J101z): these don't specifically mean eosinophilic oesophagitis.
- **Eosinophil count results:** these are lab tests, not diagnoses.

**Points to check:**
- **^ESCTEO508286 is my best guess.** I think "Eosinophilic ulcer of oesophagus" is probably another name for the same diagnosis as ^ESCTEO508265, partly because the two code numbers are close. I didn't confirm this in the tool, so check it before relying on it. Remove it if you want a stricter list.
- **The "EoE" search found nothing useful.** It only matched unrelated terms such as "tracheoesophageal" and "stereoelectroencephalography".
